jobs.description:
仿真场景搭建与资产配置:基于 NVIDIA Isaac Sim、Newton(Palatial/MuJoCo)等仿真平台,负责数字孪生场景搭建、机器人(如双臂机械臂、复合移动机器人)及物体的物理/渲染属性(USD、MJCF、Mass、Inertia、Bounds、CoACD 碰撞分解)配置与优化。
 抓取与操纵逻辑开发:负责物体抓取(Grasp Pose)、逆运动学(IK)、接触物理(Contact/Friction/Restitution)以及状态机(State Machine)逻辑的编写与测试。
 行为脚本与任务规划:编写基于 Python 的自动化行为脚本(Harness/Task Pipeline),实现“接近-抓取-抬起-振动/扰动测试-放置”等复杂离散/连续行为动作的逻辑控制与闭环校验。
 验证与指标分析:构建仿真测评 Pipeline(Metrics System),输出抓取成功率、滑移量(Contact Slide)、接触力等评估数据,并基于测试结果反向迭代 IK 与 Grasp 参数。
 算法协同与交付:与具身智能(Embodied AI)算法团队合作,为强化学习(RL)、模仿学习(Imitation Learning)或大模型部署提供高保真、稳定高并发的仿真环境与数据集生成接口。
 Real2Sim 与 Demo 生成:将第一人称视角(egocentric)等各类数据转化为高质量的 real2sim2real 仿真,用于数据集生成与 Demo 制作。
requirements: 计算机、机器人学、自动化、机电一体化等相关专业,本科及以上学历。
1 年及以上具身智能(Embodied AI)、机械臂抓取操纵或机器人仿真相关行业工作经验。
项目经验须体现机械臂抓取、灵巧手或接触操纵(manipulation)方向;仅有导航/SLAM/无人机/自动驾驶仿真经验、无操作类项目者不匹配。
精通 NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Omniverse) 或 Newton / MuJoCo 仿真框架,熟悉 USD / MJCF 物理描述文件结构。
熟悉仿真物理引擎机制(刚体动力学、接触力学、碰撞网格分解、CCD等)。
精通 Python,具备扎实的数据结构与软件工程规范,能够熟练编写面向对象的复杂逻辑脚本与自动化框架。
熟悉机器人学基础(空间变换、正/逆运动学 IK、碰撞检测算法)。
熟悉 Linux 深度开发环境、Git 版本控制与虚拟环境管理(venv / conda)。
具备严谨的调试与测试思维,能够独立追踪解决物理穿透、发散、接触抖动等仿真异常现象。
5. 英语能口头与书面沟通,能阅读英文技术文档
有 Palatial Newton、Isaac Gym 或 Brax 等高性能/并行仿真器实际项目经验者优先。
熟悉 ROS / ROS 2,具备硬件真机(如 UR、Franka、Yam 机械臂)部署或仿真到真机(Sim2Real)经验者优先。
熟悉 OpenCV、合成数据生成(SDG / Replicator)或 PBR 渲染(RTX 光线追踪、光源与材质优化)者优先。

articles.summary: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. articles.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
articles.summary: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. articles.summary: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. articles.summary: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. articles.summary: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. articles.summary: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? articles.summary: Long-horizon embodied navigation may be interrupted by a higher-priority instruction before the current task sequence is complete. articles.summary: Training robotic manipulation policies in simulation is widely adopted due to safety and cost efficiency; however, tasks involving obstacles remain under-performing and often converge slowly under Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). articles.summary: Existing manipulation data collection methods typically offer either accurate robot-state acquisition through kinematic-chain-based teleoperation or convenient, portable operation through vision-based approaches. articles.title: RoKON: Efficient and Adaptive Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Data-enabled predictive control has recently emerged as a promising control paradigm, enabling a transparent optimal-control formulation without the need to learn an explicit dynamics model. This paper presents a number of extensions paving the path towards its use in real-time robotics tasks. articles.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
articles.summary: Embodied agents are expected to accomplish real-world goals by deciding for themselves how and when to interact with their surroundings. For many such goals, changing the physical state of the world is the means rather than the end: the agent changes the state of a system through interaction, observes the feedback, and explores until it either achieves the goal itself (e.g., discovering physical laws) or learns what the goal requires; it acts to know. Manipulation benchmarks stop at acting to change, with the target state given; scientific discovery benchmarks evaluate knowing but replace physical experimentation with symbolic actions or numerical queries. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a benchmark in which a robot must act to know. articles.summary: Realizing Embodied AI for Science requires robots to translate experimental goals into reliable physical procedures, reducing hazardous and repetitive human work while generating evidence for scientific discovery. articles.summary: Dexterous manipulation of rigid objects has reached a level of maturity where grasp stability, control, and planning strategies are successfully applied in industry and logistics. articles.summary: Assistive agents in shared-control settings face a dual challenge: acting proactively to align with the human's intentions while remaining legible enough for the human to comprehend and fluently respond in real time. articles.summary: We introduce PhysLadder, a hierarchical Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation. articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are increasingly used for robot manipulation because they map camera images and a language instruction directly to actions. articles.summary: This paper presents two controllers for a quadrotor equipped with a two-DOF robot manipulator that physically interacts with the environment. articles.summary: Real robot data, rich across tasks and morphologies, is often treated as the bottleneck for training robot learning models, including embodied foundation models that aim for zero-shot physical transfer. articles.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. articles.summary: This chapter explores how robotic systems and ambient intelligence can enhance care for older adults in residential aged care (RAC) homes and private homes. articles.summary: Capturing a loose object inside a spacecraft requires a robot to approach a target that can translate and rotate, and whose motion changes when contact is made. articles.summary: Robust manipulation of soft objects, such as garments, is a critical skill for service and household robots to adopt, but remains challenging due to its high-dimensional state space, and material-dependent deformations.
